wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.description: The wallet asked about, normalised. EVM addresses come back lowercased; Solana keeps its base58 case.

chains.title: Chains
chains.description: One row per chain where this wallet exists, whether or not it has reputation there. An empty list means «not registered anywhere we index» — which is an answer, not an error.

caveats.title: Caveats
caveats.description: SUBSET of the caveats: only those computable from public data without touching the grain (today: `burn-address`, for well-known burn addresses -- nobody controls them, nobody can answer for their reputation -- and, since 2026-09-05, `thin-chain`: a chain with fewer than `reading_policy.min_raters` distinct raters on a multi-chain wallet, computable because every row here carries `distinct_raters` and `weight`). The rest of the evidence-quality set (concentration, single rater, campaign...) travels ONLY in the paid decomposition `GET /reputation/wallet/{wallet}`. An empty list here means 'no public-data caveat', NOT 'no caveats at all'.

caveats_not_computed.title: Caveats Not Computed
caveats_not_computed.description: The caveat `code`s that the paid decomposition `GET /reputation/wallet/{wallet}` evaluates and THIS free answer did not — sorted, and derived from the same module that serves `caveats`. Names only, never their outcome: whether any of them fires for this wallet is exactly what stays paid. A quality gate built on this route must treat every code listed here as unverified, not as passed.

identity_count.title: Identity Count
identity_count.description: Total ERC-8004 identities this wallet owns across every chain we read.

chains_with_identity.title: Chains With Identity
chains_with_identity.description: On how many chains it holds at least one identity.

chains_with_reputation.title: Chains With Reputation
chains_with_reputation.description: On how many of those it actually has ratings. The gap against `chains_with_identity` is registered-but-unrated, which is a different fact from unregistered.

total_reviews.title: Total Reviews
total_reviews.description: Ratings across every chain. Volume, not agreement.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: Distinct raters across the WHOLE wallet, deduplicated between chains. **Do not sum `chains[].distinct_raters`** — the same rater can rate on several chains and the sum double-counts them (measured: a wallet whose per-chain counts add to 10 has 9 real raters). `null` means the wallet is not in the ranking, which is not the same as zero raters.

WalletChains.title: WalletChains
WalletChains.description:
El mapa gratis de una wallet: identidades y reputación por cadena.

El `example` del esquema es la respuesta REAL del dominio para la wallet
del ejemplo de la ruta, leída el 2026-08-21 — su `refreshed_at` la fecha
solo. La respuesta viva es la de la propia ruta, que es gratis.

client.title: Client
client.description: Who wrote this rating: the rater's address. This is the field the whole product is about — a score without its raters is a rumor.

author_class.title: Author Class
author_class.description: Who signed this row, as a class. `facilitator-authored`: `client` is a known relayer (today the x402 facilitator's EVM wallet) that wrote the rating on behalf of the real rater, so `client` is NOT the counterparty — every such row shares one `client`, and any per-rater count merges them into one. `rater-authored`: `client` is not a relayer this index knows about; it does not prove who signed. Per rating only: no score or aggregate is computed by author class.

feedback_index.title: Feedback Index
feedback_index.description: The rater's own counter for this subject, part of the natural key `(network, agent_id, client, feedback_index)`. It is what makes re-indexing idempotent.

value.title: Value
value.description: The raw on-chain integer, untouched. Read it together with `value_decimals`; use `normalized_value` for anything comparable.

value_decimals.title: Value Decimals
value_decimals.description: Decimal places the emitter declared for `value`.

normalized_value.title: Normalized Value
normalized_value.description: `value` brought to the 0-100 domain — the only figure comparable across emitters. Null when the row is out of domain, which is also why it was excluded from the score.

tag1.title: Tag1
tag1.description: The rater's first tag: the AREA being judged (`trust`, `liveness`, `contractRisk`, `activity`, …) and, when the emitter declares it, the direction prefix. This is what `facets` are keyed by. Free vocabulary — the index carries hundreds of distinct values, so read it, never split it on `:` and hope.

tag2.title: Tag2
tag2.description: The rater's second tag, if any.

is_revoked.title: Is Revoked
is_revoked.description: The rater took this rating back. Excluded from every score, returned anyway — with `revoked_tx` — because a revocation nobody can audit is not a revocation.

is_self.title: Is Self
is_self.description: The rater IS the rated agent's current owner. Attribution, not eligibility: it travels on every row — revoked and out-of-domain included — so the breakdown says where each point came from without the caller recomputing the comparison. Self-ratings are out of every score and summarised in `self_rated`.

tx_hash.title: Tx Hash
tx_hash.description: The transaction that wrote this rating — go verify it in an explorer, which is the point. **Null until the log scan reaches this entry**, not null forever.

block_number.title: Block Number
block_number.description: Block the rating landed in. Null until the log scan dates it.

log_index.title: Log Index
log_index.description: Position within the block. Null until the log scan dates it.

feedback_uri.title: Feedback Uri
feedback_uri.description: The `feedbackURI` the standard carries — where the rater published the rating. The three `issuer*` fields below are read from it.

issuer_host.title: Issuer Host
issuer_host.description: Host of `feedback_uri`, lowercased and without `www.` — where this rating was published. Null when the rating carries no http(s) URI. Present for ~82% of the index.

issuer.title: Issuer
issuer.description: Canonical name of the issuing product when the host is a known Ultravioleta DAO service (e.g. `execution-market`), else null. Null does NOT mean unknown issuer — read `issuer_host` for that.

issuer_org.title: Issuer Org
issuer_org.description: `uvd` when this rating was written by an Ultravioleta DAO product, else null. One stable label, independent of how many products there are or what each is called.

feedback_hash.title: Feedback Hash
feedback_hash.description: Content hash the rater committed to, when it declared one.

revoked_tx.title: Revoked Tx
revoked_tx.description: The transaction that killed this rating. Without it a revocation is unauditable — which is why it travels instead of the row simply disappearing.

Rating.title: Rating
Rating.description:
One individual rating, exactly as it was written on chain.

This is the grain of the whole index — every score in this API is an
aggregate over rows of this shape, and the paid agent route returns them
one by one, revoked ones included, each with the transaction that proves
it. A revocation nobody can audit is not a revocation.
